On denotes physical surface contact/location and it a singular anaphor with unknown antecedent. Known repeated movements motivate the model rather than independently confirming it. On plus imperative press, unresolved antecedents, repeated foot/relations and differing f81r paragraph boundaries remain debts; press cannot silently become pressure, nor foot-foot both feet. No bodily-treatment genre or global winner is established.

counterpart_comparisons.claim: GDT818 fixes four sentence models by crossing solkeey=steam/basin with chedy=becomes/contains, otherwise retaining R and leaving ol unknown. evidence.quote:
The motivating ZL/IT source is unchanged:

    solkeey okaiin chedy qokain sheedy qokaiin chedaiin chealy

Two illustrative grammatical German arrangements:

- TRANSFORMATION: Dessen Dampf wird Wasser, wenn die Luft kalt ist.
- FLOW: Dessen Wasser durchfließt das Becken, wenn das Rohr offen ist.

Both require the same speculative possession and clause arrangement; five
of eight exact glosses change together. Both are completions of a known
line, not recovered sentences. Articles and German reordering are explanatory,
not separately decoded groups. RF instead has qotaiin and che@152;aiin, so
neither complete sentence transfers unchanged to that reading.

NETWORK independently proposes outlet/its/joins/channel/where/basin and
leaves the last two wholes unknown. Its relation is contact between coexisting
physical endpoints, not a change of substance or physical liquid flow.

| f77r.34 qokaiin ... chedy ... qokaiin.qokaiin | Air, pipe, foot and basin all remain repeated. No model may turn the last pair into two objects, both feet, or emphasis without a construction. FLOW also needs a flowing subject: the preceding pipe cannot automatically be it. |
| IT f77r.34 qol.chedy after an earlier chedy | In MANUAL, on-it-on; in NETWORK, joins-there-joins. Both inherit a real extra relation, not an erased word. Root's core-only TRANSFORMATION/FLOW leave qol unknown; full inherited extension retains its prior extra becomes debt. |
| f81r.20 qopchedy.qol.chedy.qokeey | Old material-source-becomes-fire; MANUAL unknown-it-on-skin; NETWORK unknown-there-joins-unknown. Different roles, but no model supplies independently identified participants. |
| f75r.35 qokain ... qokain.dar.dar | Under old water/dry this has conditional dry-water pressure. Basin/channel/hand changes remove that particular material restriction, not dar's identity or attachment. No new dar gloss is adopted. |

- f75r.32–46: TRANSFORMATION/FLOW largely offer isolated water/basin and
  one becomes/flows-through contact at .33. MANUAL gains the known central
  action pattern but leaves .34 and .45 fully unknown. NETWORK offers a
  channel at .32/.35/.40/.43 and repeated inlet at .45, not a decoded route.
- f76r.51–56: All models still lack the opening argument identities. MANUAL
  offers press-rub-press at .52 and foot...stroke-skin at .56. NETWORK's
  there at .53 and basin at .56 supply no second connected endpoint. The
  complete .55 remains unknown in all four. No wood/dry hybrid is imported.
- f77r.25–37: The two smooth .35 completions do not explain the opening,
  .29 repetition, .34 doublet or several neighbouring qualification-like
  sequences. MANUAL has rub-rub and on-hand but no complete condition. NETWORK
  has channel-its at .27 and its-outlet-joins-channel at .35 without an owner
  or translated where-tail. None yields a connected complete paragraph.
- f81r.16–31: No exact qokain or qokaiin in any reader here. All four leave
  the opening .16 unknown. TRANSFORMATION/FLOW mainly contribute predicates;
  MANUAL has stroke/press but the on-press collision; NETWORK has spatial
  anaphors without endpoints. The repeated ol groups at .22 remain unknown.

assumptions: its vapour becomes water if air is cold / its water flows through
basin if pipe is open. Five glosses change together; equal exact coverage is
not discrimination. RF has a different tail. Water/becomes are not anchors.

and BAB concrete action sequences, but f81r.27 on + imperative press is a
joint conflict. No pressure-noun rescue. NETWORK proposes channel/basin,
outlet/inlet, joins/where/there/its; no word-owned pictured endpoints.
All retain unknowns/repetitions; no complete paragraph or winner.
